questions.text: ऐल्कोहॉलों को सांद्र H2SO4 के साथ गर्म करने पर ऐल्कीन बनती हैं। अभिक्रिया का प्रथम चरण है :
questions.text_english: Alkenes are formed by heating alcohols with conc. H2SO4. The first step in the reaction is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) protonation of alcohol molecule. When an alcohol is heated with conc. H2SO4, the first step is the protonation of the -OH group of the alcohol by the strong acid H2SO4, converting -OH into -OH2+, which is a good leaving group. This protonation step must occur before any carbocation can form (option A) or water can be eliminated (option D). Formation of an ester (option B) occurs at lower temperatures and is not the first step in alkene formation.

questions.text: पॉलिहैलोजन यौगिकों का उद्योगों और कृषि में व्यापक अनुप्रयोग है। DDT भी एक अत्यंत महत्त्वपूर्ण पॉलिहैलोजन यौगिक है। यह है एक :
questions.text_english: Polyhalogen compounds have wide application in industries and agriculture. DDT is also a very important polyhalogen compound. It is a :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) non-biodegradable insecticide. DDT (Dichlorodiphenyltrichloroethane) is a polyhalogen compound that was widely used as an insecticide. It is non-biodegradable, meaning it persists in the environment and accumulates in the food chain (biomagnification), which led to its ban in many countries. It is not a greenhouse gas (A), not a fertilizer (B), and specifically not biodegradable (C), which is why it caused long-term environmental damage.

questions.text: क्षारीय माध्यम में MnO4⁻ द्वारा I⁻ के ऑक्सीकरण का उत्पाद है :
questions.text_english: The product of the oxidation of I⁻ with MnO4⁻ in alkaline medium is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) IO3⁻ (iodate ion). In alkaline medium, permanganate (MnO4⁻) is a strong oxidising agent that oxidises iodide (I⁻) to iodate (IO3⁻). MnO4⁻ itself gets reduced to MnO4²⁻ or MnO2 in alkaline conditions. In neutral or acidic medium, I⁻ would be oxidised only to I2, but in alkaline medium the oxidation goes further to IO3⁻. IO4⁻ would require even stronger conditions, and IO⁻ is an intermediate in acidic conditions.

questions.text: नीचे दी गई अभिक्रिया अनुक्रम में, Y की संरचना होगी :
questions.text_english: In the given reaction sequence, the structure of Y would be :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) Benzene. In the reaction sequence, aniline reacts with NaNO2/HCl at 0-5°C to form X, which is benzenediazonium chloride (C6H5N2+Cl⁻). When this diazonium salt is treated with ethanol (C2H5OH), the diazonium group is replaced by hydrogen through a reduction reaction, giving benzene (C6H6) as the product Y. Ethanol acts as a reducing agent in this reaction, reducing the diazonium salt to the arene. This is different from reactions with water (gives phenol) or Cu/HBF4 (gives fluorobenzene).

questions.text: 2-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन, 1-ब्रोमोब्यूटेन, 2-ब्रोमोप्रोपेन और 1-ब्रोमोप्रोपेन में से कौन-सा अणु किरेल प्रकृति का है ?
questions.text_english: Out of 2-Bromobutane, 1-Bromobutane, 2-Bromopropane and 1-Bromopropane, the molecule which is chiral in nature is :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 2-Bromobutane. A chiral molecule must have at least one asymmetric (chiral) carbon, which is a carbon atom bonded to four different groups. In 2-bromobutane (CH3CHBrCH2CH3), carbon-2 is bonded to H, Br, CH3, and CH2CH3 — four different groups, making it a chiral centre. 1-Bromobutane and 1-Bromopropane have bromine on a terminal carbon with two H atoms, so no chiral centre exists. 2-Bromopropane (CH3CHBrCH3) has carbon-2 bonded to H, Br, CH3, and CH3 — two identical groups, so it is not chiral.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित कार्बोहाइड्रेट की हॉवर्थ संरचना में विभिन्न कार्बन परमाणुओं को संख्यांकित किया गया है। ऐनोमरी कार्बन को किस संख्या से संख्यांकित किया गया है ?
questions.text_english: In the Haworth structure of the following carbohydrate, various carbon atoms have been numbered. The anomeric carbon is numbered as :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) 1. The anomeric carbon is the carbon that is generated as a new chiral centre when the open-chain form of a carbohydrate cyclises to form the ring (hemiacetal formation). In pyranose rings, this is always carbon-1, which bears the anomeric –OH group. This C-1 is the one directly attached to the ring oxygen and also carries the hydroxyl group that can be either axial (α form) or equatorial (β form). Carbon 2, 3, and 4 are ordinary ring carbons, and carbon 5 bears the CH2OH group.

questions.text: हेनरी स्थिरांक KH का मान होता है :
questions.text_english: The value of Henry's constant KH is :

options.A: उच्चतर विलेयता वाली गैसों के लिए बृहत्तर
options.B: निम्नतर विलेयता वाली गैसों के लिए बृहत्तर
options.D: गैसों की विलेयता से संबंधित नहीं है

options_english.A: greater for gases with higher solubility
options_english.B: greater for gases with lower solubility
options_english.D: not related to the solubility of gases

questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) greater for gases with lower solubility. Henry's law states that p = KH × x, where p is the partial pressure of the gas and x is its mole fraction in solution. Rearranging, x = p/KH. This means that for a given partial pressure, a larger KH results in a smaller mole fraction (lower solubility). Therefore, gases with lower solubility in a solvent have a higher value of Henry's constant KH. For example, the KH of oxygen is much higher than that of carbon dioxide, corresponding to CO2 being far more soluble in water than O2.

questions.text_english: Out of the following statements, the incorrect statement is :

options.A: La वास्तव में संक्रमण श्रेणी का तत्त्व है।
options.B: लैंथेनॉयड आकुंचन के कारण Zr और Hf की लगभग समान परमाणु त्रिज्याएँ होती हैं।
options.C: La3+ से Lu3+ आयन तक आयनिक त्रिज्या घटती है।
options.D: लैंथेनॉयड रेडियोसक्रिय प्रकृति के होते हैं।

options_english.A: La is actually an element of transition series.
options_english.B: Zr and Hf have almost identical atomic radii because of lanthanoid contraction.
options_english.C: Ionic radius decreases from La3+ to Lu3+ ion.

questions.solution: The incorrect statement is (D) Lanthanoids are radioactive in nature. Lanthanoids are NOT radioactive — it is the actinoids that are radioactive. Most lanthanoids are stable and non-radioactive elements. Statement (A) is correct: La (lanthanum, Z = 57) belongs to the d-block transition series as it has an empty 4f orbital and a d-electron. Statement (B) is correct: lanthanoid contraction causes Zr and Hf to have nearly identical atomic radii. Statement (C) is correct: ionic radius does indeed decrease from La3+ to Lu3+ due to the progressive increase in nuclear charge across the lanthanoid series.

questions.text: किसी विद्युत-रासायनिक सेल में निम्नलिखित अभिक्रिया होती है : 2Ag+(aq) + Mg(s) → 2Ag(s) + Mg2+(aq), E°सेल = 2·96 V। जैसे-जैसे अभिक्रिया आगे बढ़ती है, सेल के समग्र विभव का क्या होगा ?
questions.text_english: In an electrochemical cell, the following reaction takes place : 2Ag+(aq) + Mg(s) → 2Ag(s) + Mg2+(aq), E°cell = 2·96 V. As the reaction progresses, what will happen to the overall voltage of the cell ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) It will decrease as [Mg2+] increases. According to the Nernst equation, Ecell = E°cell – (RT/nF) ln Q. The reaction quotient Q = [Mg2+]/[Ag+]2. As the reaction progresses, [Ag+] decreases (Ag+ ions are consumed) and [Mg2+] increases (Mg2+ ions are produced), so Q increases. An increase in Q causes the cell voltage to decrease. The voltage does not remain constant (A) because concentration changes affect it. As the reaction proceeds, [Ag+] actually decreases (not increases), so option (C) is incorrect. Option (D) is wrong because an increase in [Mg2+] increases Q, which decreases, not increases, the voltage.

questions.text: Ti3+, Cr3+, Mn2+ और Ni2+ आयनों में से किसका चुम्बकीय आघूर्ण उच्चतम है ? [परमाणु क्रमांक : Ti = 22, Cr = 24, Mn = 25, Ni = 28]
questions.text_english: Out of Ti3+, Cr3+, Mn2+ and Ni2+ ions, the one which has the highest magnetic moment is : [Atomic number : Ti = 22, Cr = 24, Mn = 25, Ni = 28]
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Mn2+. The magnetic moment depends on the number of unpaired electrons by the formula μ = √(n(n+2)) BM. Ti (Z=22) has configuration [Ar]3d24s2; Ti3+ is [Ar]3d1, giving 1 unpaired electron (μ ≈ 1.73 BM). Cr (Z=24) is [Ar]3d54s1; Cr3+ is [Ar]3d3, giving 3 unpaired electrons (μ ≈ 3.87 BM). Mn (Z=25) is [Ar]3d54s2; Mn2+ is [Ar]3d5, giving 5 unpaired electrons (μ ≈ 5.92 BM). Ni (Z=28) is [Ar]3d84s2; Ni2+ is [Ar]3d8, giving 2 unpaired electrons (μ ≈ 2.83 BM). Mn2+ has the maximum of 5 unpaired electrons and therefore the highest magnetic moment.

questions.text: हॉफमान ब्रोमामाइड निम्नीकरण अभिक्रिया निम्नलिखित में से किसके द्वारा दी जाती है ?
questions.text_english: Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction is given by :
questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) CH3CONH2 (acetamide). The Hoffmann Bromamide degradation reaction requires an amide (RCONH2) as the starting material. The amide reacts with bromine in the presence of aqueous or alcoholic NaOH to give a primary amine with one carbon less than the original amide. CH3CONH2 (acetamide) undergoes this reaction to give CH3NH2 (methylamine). CH3NO2 is a nitro compound (A), CH3NH2 is already an amine and is actually the product (B), and CH3CH2NH2 is also an amine (D). Only an amide can undergo the Hoffmann degradation.

questions.text: H2O के 1 मोल को O2 में ऑक्सीकृत करने के लिए कितने विद्युत आवेश की आवश्यकता होगी ?
questions.text_english: What amount of electric charge is required for the oxidation of 1 mole of H2O to O2 ?
questions.solution: The correct answer is (B) 2F. The oxidation half-reaction at the anode during electrolysis of water is: 2H2O → O2 + 4H+ + 4e⁻. This shows that 2 moles of water produce 1 mole of O2 with the transfer of 4 electrons. Therefore, for 1 mole of H2O, the number of electrons transferred is 4/2 = 2 moles of electrons, which corresponds to a charge of 2 Faradays (2F). Each Faraday is the charge of 1 mole of electrons (96500 C), so 2F of charge is required to oxidise 1 mole of water to oxygen.

अभिकथन (A) : क्यूप्रस लवण प्रतिचुम्बकीय होते हैं।
कारण (R) : क्यूप्रस आयन में 3d-कक्षक आंशिक रूप से भरित होते हैं।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Cuprous salts are diamagnetic.
Reason (R) : In cuprous ion, 3d-orbitals are partially filled.
questions.instruction_line: सही उत्तर चुनें: (A) A और R दोनों सही, R सही व्याख्या; (B) A और R दोनों सही, R सही व्याख्या नहीं; (C) A सही, R ग़लत; (D) A ग़लत, R सही

options_english.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options_english.C: A is true, but R is false
options_english.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.solution: The correct answer is (C) Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false. Cuprous ion is Cu+ which has electronic configuration [Ar]3d10. Since all 3d orbitals are completely filled (not partially filled), there are no unpaired electrons, making cuprous salts diamagnetic. The Assertion (A) is therefore correct. However, the Reason (R) is false — 3d orbitals in Cu+ are completely filled, not partially filled. The correct reason for diamagnetism is that Cu+ has a completely filled 3d10 configuration with no unpaired electrons.

कारण (R) : ऐनिलीन के ऐसीटिलीकरण के परिणामस्वरूप नाइट्रोजन पर इलेक्ट्रॉन घनत्व घटता है।

Assertion (A) : Acetanilide is more basic than aniline.
Reason (R) : Acetylation of aniline results in decrease of electron density on nitrogen.

options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है

options_english.C: A is true, but R is false

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true. Acetanilide (C6H5NHCOCH3) is actually LESS basic than aniline, not more basic. In acetanilide, the lone pair on nitrogen is involved in resonance with the carbonyl group (–CO–), reducing the electron density on nitrogen and making it less available for protonation. Therefore, acetanilide is a weaker base than aniline. Assertion (A) is false. However, Reason (R) is correct — acetylation of aniline does indeed decrease the electron density on nitrogen because the nitrogen lone pair participates in resonance with the carbonyl group.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : जलीय NaCl का वैद्युत-अपघटन कैथोड पर H2 और ऐनोड पर Cl2 देता है।
कारण (R) : H2O की अपेक्षा क्लोरीन का ऑक्सीकरण विभव उच्चतर होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : Electrolysis of aqueous NaCl gives H2 at cathode and Cl2 at anode.
Reason (R) : Chlorine has higher oxidation potential than H2O.

options.A: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है
options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है
options.C: A सही है, परन्तु R ग़लत है
options.D: A ग़लत है, परन्तु R सही है

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options_english.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options_english.C: A is true, but R is false
options_english.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.solution: The correct answer is (A) Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A). During electrolysis of aqueous NaCl, at the cathode H2 is produced because H2O is preferentially reduced over Na+ ions. At the anode, Cl2 is produced despite the presence of OH⁻ ions from water, because Cl⁻ ions have a higher oxidation potential (lower reduction potential) than OH⁻/H2O. This means Cl⁻ is oxidised more easily, producing Cl2 at the anode. The Reason (R) correctly explains why Cl2 is preferentially produced at the anode over O2 from water.

अभिकथन (A) : n-ब्यूटिल ब्रोमाइड की तुलना में n-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड का क्वथनांक उच्चतर होता है।
कारण (R) : C–Br आबंध की तुलना में C–Cl आबंध अधिक ध्रुवीय होता है।
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A) : n-Butyl chloride has higher boiling point than n-Butyl bromide.
Reason (R) : C–Cl bond is more polar than C–Br bond.

options.A: A और R दोनों सही हैं और R, A की सही व्याख्या करता है
options.B: A और R दोनों सही हैं, परन्तु R, A की सही व्याख्या नहीं करता है
options.C: A सही है, परन्तु R ग़लत है
options.D: A ग़लत है, परन्तु R सही है

options_english.A: Both A and R are true and R is the correct explanation of A
options_english.B: Both A and R are true, but R is not the correct explanation of A
options_english.C: A is true, but R is false
options_english.D: A is false, but R is true

questions.solution: The correct answer is (D) Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true. n-Butyl bromide actually has a HIGHER boiling point than n-butyl chloride (n-BuBr bp ≈ 102°C vs n-BuCl bp ≈ 78°C). The boiling point of haloalkanes increases as we go from chloride to bromide to iodide in the same series, because the London dispersion forces (van der Waals forces) increase with increasing molecular size and polarisability. The bromine atom is larger and more polarisable than chlorine, leading to stronger intermolecular forces and a higher boiling point. Assertion (A) is therefore false. However, Reason (R) is true — C–Cl bond is indeed more polar than C–Br bond since chlorine is more electronegative than bromine.

questions.text: आवश्यक ऐमीनो अम्लों से क्या अभिप्राय है ? ऐमीनो अम्ल उभयधर्मी प्रकृति के क्यों होते हैं ?
questions.text_english: What is meant by essential amino acids ? Why are amino acids amphoteric in nature ?

key_points: Essential amino acids are those that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be obtained through diet.
Amino acids are amphoteric because they contain both an acidic group (-COOH) and a basic group (-NH2) in the same molecule.

questions.solution: Essential amino acids are those amino acids that cannot be synthesised by the human body and must be supplied through the diet. Examples include valine, leucine, lysine, and phenylalanine. Amino acids are amphoteric in nature because they possess both an acidic carboxyl group (–COOH) and a basic amino group (–NH2) in the same molecule. In solution, the –COOH group can donate a proton (acting as an acid), while the –NH2 group can accept a proton (acting as a base). As a result, amino acids can react with both acids and bases, and they exist in aqueous solution mainly as zwitterions (H3N+–CHR–COO⁻).

questions.text: (क) किसी अभिकारक 'A' का अपघटन होता है। 'A' की सांद्रता की माप निश्चित अंतराल पर की गई जिसे नीचे दी गई सारणी में अंकित किया गया : समय/घंटे: 0, 1, 2, 3 | [A]/M: 0·40, 0·20, 0·10, 0·05 | ऊपर दिए गए आँकड़ों के आधार पर, अभिक्रिया की कोटि की प्रागुक्ति कीजिए और इसके वेग नियम का व्यंजक लिखिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Reactant 'A' underwent a decomposition reaction. The concentration of 'A' was measured periodically and recorded in the table given below : Time/Hours: 0, 1, 2, 3 | [A]/M: 0·40, 0·20, 0·10, 0·05. Based on the above data, predict the order of the reaction and write the expression for the rate law.

sub_questions.text: (ख) H2(g) और I2(g) के बीच अभिक्रिया एक बन्द समतापी पात्र में की गई। अभिक्रिया के लिए वेग नियम पाया गया : वेग = k[H2][I2]। ताप को स्थिर रखते हुए यदि अभिक्रिया कोष्ठ में 1 मोल H2(g) मिलाई गई, तो अभिक्रिया वेग तथा वेग स्थिरांक में परिवर्तन की प्रागुक्ति कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) The reaction between H2(g) and I2(g) was carried out in a sealed isothermal container. The rate law for the reaction was found to be : Rate = k[H2][I2]. If 1 mole of H2(g) was added to the reaction chamber and the temperature was kept constant, then predict the change in rate of the reaction and the rate constant.

key_points: Adding more H2 increases [H2], so rate increases.
Rate constant k depends only on temperature; since temperature is constant, k remains unchanged.

sub_questions.solution: When 1 mole of H2(g) is added to the sealed container at constant temperature, the concentration [H2] increases. Since Rate = k[H2][I2], the rate of the reaction will increase because [H2] has increased while [I2] remains unchanged. However, the rate constant k depends only on temperature (as given by the Arrhenius equation), and since the temperature is kept constant, the rate constant k will remain unchanged.

key_points: The concentration halves every hour, indicating a first-order reaction.
Rate law: Rate = k[A]

questions.solution: From the data, the concentration of A halves every hour: 0.40 → 0.20 → 0.10 → 0.05 M. This constant half-life (t½ = 1 hour) is characteristic of a first-order reaction. Therefore, the reaction is of first order. The rate law expression is: Rate = k[A], where k is the first-order rate constant. The half-life for a first-order reaction is t½ = 0.693/k, giving k = 0.693 h⁻1.

questions.text: PtCl4·2KCl, AgNO3 विलयन के साथ AgCl का अवक्षेप नहीं देता है। संकुल का संरचनात्मक सूत्र और IUPAC नाम लिखिए।
questions.text_english: PtCl4·2KCl doesn't give precipitate of AgCl with AgNO3 solution. Write the structural formula and IUPAC name of the complex.

key_points: Structural formula: K2[PtCl4] — all chloride ions are inside the coordination sphere.
IUPAC name: Potassium tetrachloridoplatinate(II)

questions.solution: Since PtCl4·2KCl does not give a precipitate of AgCl with AgNO3 solution, it means all the Cl⁻ ions are present inside the coordination sphere and are not free ions in solution. The structural formula of the complex is K2[PtCl4], where Pt(II) is the central metal ion coordinated to four Cl⁻ ligands, and two K+ ions are the counter ions in the outer sphere. The IUPAC name of the complex is Potassium tetrachloridoplatinate(II). Here, Pt has an oxidation state of +2 (since 4 Cl⁻ ions contribute –4 and 2 K+ contribute +2, giving Pt = +2).

questions.text: ईंधन सेल को परिभाषित कीजिए। साधारण सेल की तुलना में ईंधन सेल के दो लाभ दीजिए।
questions.text_english: Define fuel cell. Give two advantages of fuel cell over ordinary cell.

key_points: A fuel cell is a galvanic cell in which the energy of combustion of fuels is directly converted into electrical energy.
Advantage 1: Higher efficiency (up to 70%) compared to ordinary cells.
Advantage 2: No pollution as the product is water (in H2-O2 fuel cell); fuel can be continuously supplied.

questions.solution: A fuel cell is a type of galvanic cell in which the chemical energy from the continuous combustion of a fuel (such as hydrogen or methane) is directly converted into electrical energy. Unlike ordinary batteries, the reactants (fuel and oxidant) are continuously fed into the cell and the products are continuously removed. Two advantages of fuel cells over ordinary cells are: first, fuel cells have much higher energy conversion efficiency (up to 70%) since they convert chemical energy directly into electrical energy without involving heat, whereas ordinary cells have lower efficiency; second, fuel cells cause less pollution — for example, the hydrogen-oxygen fuel cell produces only water as a by-product, making it environmentally clean, whereas ordinary cells involve disposal of toxic chemicals.

questions.text_english: Write the structures of the main products of the following reactions : (a) 6R-C(R)(R)-OH + 2Al → ; (b) [cyclohexyl-CH2-C(=O)-OCH3] + NaBH4 →

key_points: Product: 2Al(OCRRR)3, i.e., aluminium alkoxide

sub_questions.solution: When a tertiary alcohol (R3COH) reacts with aluminium metal, it forms an aluminium alkoxide. The product is Al(OCRR'R'')3, i.e., tris(trialkylmethoxy)aluminium or aluminium trialkoxide: 2Al + 6R3COH → 2Al(OCR3)3 + 3H2↑. The main product is aluminium trialkoxide [Al(OCRRR)3] and hydrogen gas is evolved.

key_points: NaBH4 selectively reduces the ester group; product is the corresponding alcohol: cyclohexyl-CH2-CH2OH and methanol (or the hemiacetal product depending on conditions). Actually NaBH4 does NOT reduce esters; only the ketone/aldehyde if present. This molecule has an ester, so NaBH4 does not react with it significantly.

sub_questions.solution: NaBH4 is a mild reducing agent that selectively reduces aldehydes and ketones but does NOT reduce esters under normal conditions. In the given compound (a cyclohexane ring bearing a –CH2–C(=O)–O–CH3 group, which is methyl ester of a carboxymethyl-cyclohexane), there is no aldehyde or ketone carbonyl present — only an ester group. Therefore, NaBH4 does not react with this ester. The compound remains unchanged. (Note: If the intended structure contains a ketone carbonyl in addition, NaBH4 would reduce only that carbonyl to give the corresponding secondary alcohol, leaving the ester intact.)

key_points: Part (a): aluminium alkoxide is formed
Part (b): NaBH4 selectively reduces carbonyl (ketone/aldehyde) but not ester

questions.solution: Part (a): When a tertiary alcohol (R3COH) reacts with aluminium, the product is aluminium trialkoxide Al(OCR3)3 along with hydrogen gas: 2Al + 6R3COH → 2Al(OCR3)3 + 3H2. Part (b): NaBH4 is a selective reducing agent that reduces aldehydes and ketones but does not reduce ester groups under normal conditions. In the given molecule (cyclohexyl methyl ester), only an ester carbonyl is present, which NaBH4 does not reduce. Hence the compound remains unchanged under NaBH4 treatment.

questions.text: (क) क्या तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल मेथिल ईथर बनाने के लिए सोडियम मेथॉक्साइड और तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल ब्रोमाइड का उपयोग किया जा सकता है? उचित कारण दीजिए। तृतीयक-ब्यूटिल मेथिल ईथर बनाने के लिए आवश्यक उपयुक्त प्रारम्भिक पदार्थों का सुझाव देते हुए अपने उत्तर का औचित्य दीजिए। (ख) ऊपर उल्लिखित ईथर का IUPAC नाम दीजिए।
questions.text_english: (a) Can sodium methoxide and t-butyl bromide be used for the preparation of t-butyl methyl ether. Give suitable reason. Justify your answer by suggesting the appropriate starting material if required for the preparation of t-butyl methyl ether. (b) Give the IUPAC name of above mentioned ether.

sub_questions.text: (क) क्या सोडियम मेथॉक्साइड और t-ब्यूटिल ब्रोमाइड का उपयोग किया जा सकता है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Can sodium methoxide and t-butyl bromide be used for the preparation of t-butyl methyl ether?

key_points: No, because t-butyl bromide is a tertiary alkyl halide which undergoes elimination (E2) with a strong base like sodium methoxide instead of substitution (SN2).
Correct method: Use methyl bromide (CH3Br) and sodium t-butoxide (NaOC(CH3)3) via Williamson synthesis.

sub_questions.solution: No, sodium methoxide and t-butyl bromide cannot be used for the preparation of t-butyl methyl ether. This is because t-butyl bromide is a tertiary alkyl halide, and when it reacts with a strong base/nucleophile like sodium methoxide (CH3ONa), the bulky tertiary substrate undergoes elimination (E2 reaction) predominantly rather than nucleophilic substitution (SN2), giving isobutylene (2-methylpropene) as the major product instead of the desired ether. To prepare t-butyl methyl ether, we should use the Williamson synthesis with sodium t-butoxide (NaOC(CH3)3) and methyl bromide (CH3Br), since methyl bromide is a primary alkyl halide that undergoes SN2 smoothly without elimination.

sub_questions.text: (ख) ऊपर उल्लिखित ईथर का IUPAC नाम दीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Give the IUPAC name of above mentioned ether.

key_points: 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane

sub_questions.solution: The IUPAC name of t-butyl methyl ether (CH3–O–C(CH3)3) is 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane. The longest carbon chain containing the oxygen substituent is selected as the parent chain (propane with 3 carbons of the t-butyl group), and the methoxy group (–OCH3) is treated as a substituent at carbon 2.

key_points: Cannot use NaOCH3 + t-BuBr; elimination occurs instead
Use NaOC(CH3)3 + CH3Br for Williamson synthesis
IUPAC name: 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane

questions.solution: Part (a): Sodium methoxide and t-butyl bromide cannot be used together to make t-butyl methyl ether because the tertiary alkyl halide (t-BuBr) undergoes E2 elimination preferentially with the strong base CH3ONa, yielding isobutylene rather than the ether. The correct approach via Williamson synthesis is to use sodium t-butoxide (NaOC(CH3)3) with methyl bromide (CH3Br), a primary halide that readily undergoes SN2. Part (b): The IUPAC name of t-butyl methyl ether (CH3OC(CH3)3) is 2-methoxy-2-methylpropane.

questions.text: पूछे गए अनुसार निम्नलिखित यौगिकों को व्यवस्थित कीजिए : (क) C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C6H5NHCH3, C6H5NH2 को pKb मानों के बढ़ते हुए क्रम में; (ख) C2H5OH, C2H5NH2, (CH3)2NH को क्वथनांक के घटते हुए क्रम में; (ग) C6H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C2H5NH2 को जल में विलेयता के घटते हुए क्रम में।
questions.text_english: Arrange the following compounds as asked : (a) in increasing order of pKb values: C2H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C6H5NHCH3, C6H5NH2; (b) in decreasing order of boiling point: C2H5OH, C2H5NH2, (CH3)2NH; (c) in decreasing order of solubility in water: C6H5NH2, (C2H5)2NH, C2H5NH2.

key_points: (a) Increasing pKb (i.e. decreasing basicity): C6H5NH2 < C6H5NHCH3 < C2H5NH2 < (C2H5)2NH
(b) Decreasing boiling point: C2H5OH > C2H5NH2 > (CH3)2NH
(c) Decreasing solubility in water: C2H5NH2 > (C2H5)2NH > C6H5NH2

questions.solution: Part (a) – Increasing pKb (decreasing basicity): C6H5NH2 (aniline, lone pair delocalised in ring, weakest base, highest pKb = 9.4) < C6H5NHCH3 (N-methylaniline, slightly more basic than aniline due to +I of methyl) < C2H5NH2 (ethylamine, aliphatic, strongly basic, low pKb ≈ 3.3) < (C2H5)2NH (diethylamine, two ethyl groups donate electrons, most basic, lowest pKb ≈ 3.0). So order of increasing pKb: (C2H5)2NH < C2H5NH2 < C6H5NHCH3 < C6H5NH2. Part (b) – Decreasing boiling point: C2H5OH (bp 78°C, strong H-bonding with O) > C2H5NH2 (bp 17°C, moderate N–H bonding) > (CH3)2NH (bp 7°C, only one N–H bond, weaker intermolecular forces). Part (c) – Decreasing solubility in water: C2H5NH2 (fully miscible, small size, H-bonding) > (C2H5)2NH (moderately soluble, larger hydrophobic part) > C6H5NH2 (aniline, least soluble, large aromatic ring reduces solubility).

questions.text: 25°C पर निम्नलिखित अर्ध-सेलों को जोड़कर बने वोल्टीय सेल का सेल विभव परिकलित कीजिए : Al/Al3+ (0·001 M) और Ni/Ni2+ (0·001 M)। दिया गया है : E°(Ni2+/Ni) = –0·25 V, E°(Al3+/Al) = –1·66 V।
questions.text_english: Calculate the cell voltage of the voltaic cell which is set up by joining the following half-cells at 25°C : Al/Al3+ (0·001 M) and Ni/Ni2+ (0·001 M). Given : E°(Ni2+/Ni) = –0·25 V, E°(Al3+/Al) = –1·66 V.

key_points: Al is anode (more negative E°), Ni is cathode.
E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = (–0.25) – (–1.66) = +1.41 V
Applying Nernst equation with n = 6: Ecell = 1.41 – (0.0592/6) log([Al3+]3/[Ni2+]2) = 1.41 V (concentrations equal, so correction = 0)

questions.solution: Since E°(Al3+/Al) = –1.66 V is more negative than E°(Ni2+/Ni) = –0.25 V, aluminium acts as the anode (oxidation) and nickel acts as the cathode (reduction). The cell reaction is: 2Al(s) + 3Ni2+(aq) → 2Al3+(aq) + 3Ni(s). E°cell = E°cathode – E°anode = (–0.25) – (–1.66) = +1.41 V. Using the Nernst equation with n = 6 electrons transferred: Ecell = E°cell – (0.0592/6) × log([Al3+]2/[Ni2+]3). Substituting [Al3+] = 0.001 M and [Ni2+] = 0.001 M: log((0.001)2/(0.001)3) = log(0.001⁻1) = log(1000) = 3. Therefore, Ecell = 1.41 – (0.0592/6) × 3 = 1.41 – 0.0296 = 1.38 V (approximately).

questions.text: (क) निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए : (i) n-प्रोपिल क्लोराइड की तुलना में ऐलिल क्लोराइड अधिक तीव्रता से जल-अपघटित होता है। (ii) ऐल्किल हैलाइडों को जब सिल्वर सायनाइड के साथ अभिक्रियित किया जाता है तब आइसोसायनाइड बनते हैं। (iii) SN2 अभिक्रिया में t-ब्यूटिल क्लोराइड की तुलना में मेथिल क्लोराइड OH⁻ आयन के साथ अधिक शीघ्रता से अभिक्रिया करता है।
questions.text_english: (a) Account for the following : (i) Allyl chloride is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride. (ii) Isocyanides are formed when alkyl halides are treated with silver cyanide. (iii) Methyl chloride reacts faster with OH⁻ ion in SN2 reaction than t-butyl chloride.

sub_questions.text: (ख) 'A' और 'B' के संरचनात्मक सूत्र लिखकर निम्नलिखित अभिक्रियाओं को पूर्ण कीजिए : (i) CH3CH=CH2 + HBr (परॉक्साइड) → 'A' + जलीय KOH → 'B'; (ii) CH3CH2CHCH3(Cl) + ऐल्कोहॉलिक KOH → 'A' + HBr → 'B'; (iii) 'A' + Mg → CH3CH2MgCl, CH3CH2MgCl + H2O/H+ → 'B' (मुख्य उत्पाद)
sub_questions.text_english: (b) Complete the following reactions by writing the structural formulae of 'A' and 'B' : (i) CH3CH=CH2 + HBr/Peroxide → 'A' + aq.KOH → 'B'; (ii) CH3CH2CHCH3(Cl) + alc.KOH → 'A' + HBr → 'B'; (iii) 'A' + Mg → CH3CH2MgCl, + H2O/H+ → 'B' (main product)

key_points: (i) A = CH3CH2CH2Br (anti-Markovnikov addition); B = CH3CH2CH2OH
(ii) A = CH3CH=CHCH3 (but-2-ene, Saytzeff); B = CH3CH(Br)CHCH3 (sec-2-bromobutane)
(iii) A = CH3CH2Cl (chloroethane); B = CH3CH3 (ethane, from Grignard + water)

sub_questions.solution: Reaction (i): CH3CH=CH2 reacts with HBr in the presence of peroxide via free radical addition (anti-Markovnikov): A = CH3CH2CH2Br (1-bromopropane). Then A reacts with aq. KOH (SN2 hydrolysis): B = CH3CH2CH2OH (1-propanol). Reaction (ii): CH3CH2CH(Cl)CH3 reacts with alc. KOH under heat (elimination, Saytzeff rule): A = CH3CH=CHCH3 (but-2-ene, major product). Then A reacts with HBr (Markovnikov addition): B = CH3CH(Br)CH2CH3 (2-bromobutane). Reaction (iii): 'A' reacts with Mg to give CH3CH2MgCl (ethyl magnesium chloride), so A = CH3CH2Cl (chloroethane). CH3CH2MgCl reacts with H2O/H+: B = CH3CH3 (ethane, as the Grignard reagent is protonated by water).

key_points: (i) Allyl chloride undergoes resonance stabilisation of the carbocation/SN1 transition state, making it easier to hydrolyse.
(ii) AgCN is a covalent compound; C–Ag bond ionic, so carbon attacks through nitrogen, giving isocyanide (R–N≡C:).
(iii) SN2 rate depends on steric hindrance; methyl chloride (no bulky groups) reacts much faster than t-butyl chloride (three methyl groups block backside attack).

questions.solution: (i) Allyl chloride (CH2=CHCH2Cl) is hydrolysed more readily than n-propyl chloride because the carbocation formed after ionisation of allyl chloride (allylic carbocation, CH2=CH–CH2+) is stabilised by resonance with the double bond, lowering the activation energy. n-Propyl chloride forms a primary carbocation with no resonance stabilisation, making ionisation much more difficult. (ii) Silver cyanide (AgCN) is a covalent compound where silver is bonded to nitrogen (Ag–N≡C). When alkyl halides react with AgCN, the carbon of the alkyl halide bonds to the nitrogen end of cyanide, producing isocyanides (R–N+≡C⁻). If KCN were used (ionic, C-end attacks), cyanides would form. (iii) In an SN2 reaction, the nucleophile attacks from the back of the carbon bearing the leaving group. Methyl chloride has no steric hindrance, allowing easy backside attack by OH⁻. t-Butyl chloride has three bulky methyl groups around the reaction centre, severely hindering the approach of the nucleophile, so SN2 is extremely slow for t-BuCl.

questions.text: निम्नलिखित प्रत्येक प्रेक्षण के लिए स्पष्टीकरण दीजिए : (क) Mn3+ आयन ऑक्सीकारक है जबकि Cr2+ आयन अपचायक है यद्यपि दोनों का d-कक्षक विन्यास (d4) एक समान है। (ख) लैंथेनॉयड आकुंचन की तुलना में एक तत्त्व से दूसरे तत्त्व के बीच ऐक्टिनॉयड आकुंचन अधिक होता है। (ग) H, B, C और N के साथ संक्रमण धातुएँ बहुत अधिक संख्या में अंतराकाशी यौगिक बनाती हैं।
questions.text_english: Give explanation for each of the following observations : (a) With the same d-orbital configuration (d4), Mn3+ ion is an oxidising agent whereas Cr2+ ion is a reducing agent. (b) Actinoid contraction is greater from element to element than that among lanthanoids. (c) Transition metals form large number of interstitial compounds with H, B, C and N.

key_points: (a) Mn3+ (d4) tends to gain an electron to reach the more stable d5 half-filled configuration (Mn2+), so it acts as an oxidising agent. Cr2+ (d4) tends to lose an electron to reach the stable d3 configuration (Cr3+ with half-filled t2g), so it acts as a reducing agent.
(b) 5f orbitals of actinoids are more diffuse and offer poorer shielding of nuclear charge than 4f orbitals of lanthanoids, resulting in greater effective nuclear charge increase per element.
(c) Transition metals have small atomic radii and many voids in their crystal lattice; small atoms of H, B, C, N can fit into these interstitial voids.

questions.solution: Part (a): Both Mn3+ and Cr2+ have d4 configuration, but they show opposite behaviour. Mn3+ (d4) acts as an oxidising agent because gaining one electron gives it the d5 configuration (half-filled, extra stability by Hund's rule), driving it to get reduced. Cr2+ (d4) acts as a reducing agent because losing one electron gives it d3 (t2g3, half-filled t2g sub-shell, extra stability in an octahedral field), making it tend to be oxidised. Part (b): In actinoids, the 5f orbitals are more spatially diffuse and provide poorer shielding of the nuclear charge compared to the 4f orbitals of lanthanoids. Therefore, as protons are added across the actinoid series, the effective nuclear charge experienced by outer electrons increases more sharply, causing a greater contraction in atomic/ionic radius per element than in lanthanoids. Part (c): Transition metals have close-packed crystal structures with small interstitial voids. The atoms of H, B, C, and N are very small and can occupy these voids without significantly distorting the metallic lattice, forming interstitial (non-stoichiometric) compounds. These interstitial compounds are harder, have higher melting points, and retain metallic conductivity.

questions.text: NaOH का एक जलीय विलयन बनाया गया और परासरण दाब की माप से 27°C पर इसका मोलर द्रव्यमान 25 g mol⁻1 पाया गया। इस विलयन में NaOH का प्रतिशत वियोजन परिकलित कीजिए। [परमाणु द्रव्यमान : Na = 23 u, O = 16 u, H = 1 u]
questions.text_english: An aqueous solution of NaOH was made and its molar mass from the measurement of osmotic pressure at 27°C was found to be 25 g mol⁻1. Calculate the percentage dissociation of NaOH in this solution. [Atomic mass : Na = 23 u, O = 16 u, H = 1 u]

key_points: Molar mass of NaOH = 40 g/mol
Van't Hoff factor i = M(normal)/M(observed) = 40/25 = 1.6
For NaOH → Na+ + OH⁻, i = 1 + α = 1.6, so α = 0.6, percentage dissociation = 60%

questions.solution: The molar mass of NaOH = 23 + 16 + 1 = 40 g mol⁻1. The observed molar mass from osmotic pressure measurements is 25 g mol⁻1. The van’t Hoff factor i = M(normal)/M(observed) = 40/25 = 1.6. NaOH dissociates as: NaOH → Na+ + OH⁻. If α is the degree of dissociation, then: i = 1 + α(2 − 1) = 1 + α. Therefore, 1 + α = 1.6, giving α = 0.6. The percentage dissociation of NaOH = α × 100 = 0.6 × 100 = 60%.

questions.text: C4H8O आण्विक सूत्र वाला कोई यौगिक 'A' धनात्मक 2,4-DNP परीक्षण देता है। यह सोडियम हाइपोआयोडाइट के साथ अभिक्रियित किए जाने पर यौगिक 'B' का पीला अवक्षेप देता है। यौगिक 'A' टॉलेन अथवा फेलिंग अभिकमाक के साथ अभिक्रिया नहीं करता है; KMnO4 के साथ प्रबल ऑक्सीकरण पर यह कार्बोक्सिलिक अम्ल 'C' बनाता है। 'A', 'B' और 'C' की संरचनाएँ स्पष्ट कीजिए। उनके IUPAC नाम भी दीजिए।
questions.text_english: A compound 'A' with molecular formula C4H8O gives positive 2,4-DNP test. It gives yellow precipitate of compound 'B' on treatment with sodium hypoiodite. Compound 'A' does not react with Tollen's or Fehling's reagent; on drastic oxidation with KMnO4, it forms a carboxylic acid 'C'. Elucidate the structures of 'A', 'B' and 'C'. Also give their IUPAC names.

key_points: A = CH3COCH2CH3 (butanone / methyl ethyl ketone)
B = CHI3 (iodoform, yellow precipitate)
C = CH3COOH (ethanoic/acetic acid) from oxidation of methyl ketone

questions.solution: Compound 'A' (C4H8O) gives a positive 2,4-DNP test, confirming the presence of a carbonyl group (C=O), so it is either an aldehyde or a ketone. Since it does not react with Tollen's or Fehling's reagent, it is not an aldehyde but a ketone. It gives a yellow precipitate (iodoform, CHI3) with NaOI (the iodoform test), which indicates it is a methyl ketone (CH3CO– group). From C4H8O with the CH3CO– group, the remaining fragment is C2H5–, so A = CH3COCH2CH3 (butanone or methyl ethyl ketone). Its IUPAC name is butan-2-one. Compound 'B' is CHI3 (iodoform), IUPAC name triiodomethane — a yellow solid. On drastic oxidation of butanone with KMnO4, the C–CO bond is cleaved to give ethanoic acid (CH3COOH) as compound 'C'. The IUPAC name of C is ethanoic acid.

questions.text: राइबोस और 2-डिऑक्सीराइबोस की जीव विज्ञान में महत्त्वपूर्ण भूमिका है। उनके सबसे महत्त्वपूर्ण व्युत्पन्न वे हैं जिनमें फ़ॉस्फेट समूह 5-स्थिति से बँधता है। मोनो-, डाई- और ट्राई-फ़ॉस्फेट रूप तथा 3-5 चक्रीय मोनोफ़ॉस्फेट महत्त्वपूर्ण हैं। प्यूरीन और पिरिमिडीन, राइबोस तथा डिऑक्सीराइबोस के साथ यौगिकों का एक मुख्य वर्ग बनाते हैं। जब ये प्यूरीन और पिरिमिडीन व्युत्पन्न राइबोस शर्करा के साथ युग्मन करते हैं, तो ये न्यूक्लियोसाइड कहलाते हैं।
questions.text_english: Ribose and 2-deoxyribose have an important role in biology. Among the most important derivatives are those with phosphate groups attached at the 5 position. Mono-, di- and tri-phosphate forms are important, as well as 3-5 cyclic monophosphates. Purines and pyrimidines form an important class of compounds with ribose and deoxyribose. When these purine and pyrimidine derivatives are coupled to a ribose sugar, they are called nucleosides.

sub_questions.text: (क) जब DNA को जल-अपघटित किया जाता है तो क्या उत्पाद बनेंगे ? संरचना के संदर्भ में DNA किस प्रकार RNA से भिन्न है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) What products would be formed when DNA is hydrolysed ? How is DNA different from RNA with reference to a structure ?

key_points: Hydrolysis of DNA gives: phosphoric acid, 2-deoxyribose sugar, and four nitrogenous bases (adenine, guanine, cytosine, thymine).
Structural difference: DNA contains 2-deoxyribose sugar and thymine base; RNA contains ribose sugar and uracil instead of thymine. Also DNA is double-stranded; RNA is usually single-stranded.

sub_questions.solution: When DNA is hydrolysed, it produces three types of components: phosphoric acid (H3PO4), the pentose sugar 2-deoxyribose, and four nitrogenous bases — adenine (A), guanine (G), cytosine (C), and thymine (T). Structurally, DNA differs from RNA in two ways: first, DNA contains 2-deoxyribose as its sugar component, while RNA contains ribose (which has an –OH group at the 2’ position); second, DNA contains the base thymine (T), which is replaced by uracil (U) in RNA. Additionally, DNA is usually double-stranded with a double helix structure, whereas RNA is generally single-stranded.

sub_questions.text: (ख) न्यूक्लियोटाइड और न्यूक्लियोसाइड में अंतर स्पष्ट कीजिए।

key_points: Nucleoside = nitrogenous base + sugar (no phosphate).
Nucleotide = nitrogenous base + sugar + phosphate group.

sub_questions.solution: A nucleoside consists of a nitrogenous base (purine or pyrimidine) linked to a pentose sugar (ribose or deoxyribose) through an N-glycosidic bond — it has no phosphate group. A nucleotide is a nucleoside that additionally has one or more phosphate groups esterified at the 5’-OH of the sugar. In other words, nucleotide = nucleoside + phosphate group. Nucleotides are the monomeric units of nucleic acids (DNA and RNA), while nucleosides are obtained when the phosphate group is removed.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(i) न्यूक्लीक अम्ल के दो महत्त्वपूर्ण प्रकार्यों का उल्लेख कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c)(i) Mention two important functions of nucleic acid.

key_points: 1. Storage and transmission of genetic information from one generation to the next (DNA).
2. Control of protein synthesis in the cell (RNA directs translation).

sub_questions.solution: Two important functions of nucleic acids are: (1) Storage and transmission of genetic information — DNA stores the hereditary information of an organism and transmits it from parents to offspring during cell division and reproduction. (2) Protein synthesis — RNA (particularly mRNA, tRNA and rRNA) controls the synthesis of proteins in the cell by transcribing the genetic code from DNA and translating it into specific amino acid sequences during translation at the ribosome.

sub_questions.text: (ग)(ii) दो न्यूक्लियोटाइडों को जोड़ने वाले बंध का नाम बताइए। उस क्षारक का नाम लिखिए जो RNA के न्यूक्लियोटाइड में पाया जाता है लेकिन DNA में नहीं।
sub_questions.text_english: (c)(ii) Name the linkage which joins two nucleotides. Name the base that is found in nucleotide of RNA but not in DNA.

key_points: Linkage: phosphodiester bond (3’-5’ phosphodiester linkage)
Base in RNA but not DNA: Uracil (U)

sub_questions.solution: The two nucleotides in a nucleic acid chain are joined by a 3’-5’ phosphodiester bond, also called a phosphodiester linkage. This bond is formed between the 3’-OH of one nucleotide's sugar and the 5’-phosphate of the next nucleotide. The nitrogenous base that is found in the nucleotides of RNA but not in DNA is uracil (U). In DNA, uracil is replaced by thymine (5-methyluracil). Both thymine and uracil pair with adenine through hydrogen bonding.

questions.text: आदर्श विलयन की सामान्यतः स्वीकृत परिभाषा के अनुसार उसी अथवा भिन्न स्पीशीज़ के अणुओं के मध्य समान अन्योन्यक्रिया बल कार्य करते हैं। (यह कथन तुल्य है कि घटकों की सक्रियता उनकी सांद्रता के बराबर होती है।) सच पूछिए तो यह शर्त मिश्रणों (ध्रुवण समावयव, तत्त्व के समस्थानिक मिश्रणों, हाइड्रोकार्बन मिश्रणों) के लिए केवल अपवादात्मक प्रकरणों में ही पूरी होती है। आदर्श विलयनों के विषय में सीमित प्रकरणों में ही चर्चा की जा सकती है क्योंकि विलायक के संदर्भ में अत्यंत तनु विलयन ही आदर्शतः व्यवहार करते हैं। इस दृष्टिकोण को इस तथ्य से और भी समर्थन मिला कि राउल्ट नियम ने तनु विलयनों में विलायक के व्यवहार का वर्णन करने के लिए आनुभविक रूप से ज्ञात किया तथा पूर्वधारणा के माध्यम से ऊष्मागतिकी द्वारा विलायक के आदर्श व्यवहार को निगमित किया जा सकता है।
questions.text_english: According to the generally accepted definition of the ideal solution there are equal interaction forces acting between molecules belonging to the same or different species. (This is equivalent to the statement that the activity of the components equals the concentration.) Strictly speaking, this condition is fulfilled only in exceptional cases for mixtures (optical isomers, isotopic mixtures of an element, hydrocarbon mixtures). It is still usual to talk about ideal solutions as limiting cases in reality since very dilute solutions behave ideally with respect to the solvent. This view is further supported by the fact that Raoult's law empirically found for describing the behaviour of the solvent in dilute solutions can be deduced thermodynamically via the assumption of ideal behaviour of the solvent.

sub_questions.text: (क) मिश्रणीय द्रव युगल का एक उदाहरण दीजिए जो राउल्ट नियम से ऋणात्मक विचलन दर्शाता है। इस विचलन का क्या कारण है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (a) Give one example of miscible liquid pair which shows negative deviation from Raoult's law. What is the reason for such deviation ?

key_points: Example: Acetone and chloroform (or water and HCl, or water and HNO3).
Reason: The A-B intermolecular interactions are stronger than the A-A and B-B interactions, so the vapour pressure is lower than predicted by Raoult's law.

sub_questions.solution: A common example of a miscible liquid pair showing negative deviation from Raoult's law is acetone and chloroform. The reason for negative deviation is that the intermolecular interactions between acetone and chloroform molecules (A–B type) are stronger than the interactions between similar molecules alone (A–A or B–B type). This happens because a hydrogen bond forms between the –H of CHCl3 and the –C=O of acetone. As a result, the tendency of molecules to escape into vapour (vapour pressure) is reduced below what Raoult's law predicts. The total vapour pressure of the mixture is therefore less than the ideal value, giving a negative deviation.

sub_questions.text: (ख)(i) वाष्पशील अवयवों वाले विलयन के लिए राउल्ट नियम बताइए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b)(i) State Raoult's law for a solution containing volatile components.

key_points: For each volatile component, partial vapour pressure = mole fraction × vapour pressure of pure component. Total pressure = sum of partial pressures.

sub_questions.solution: Raoult's law for a solution containing volatile components states that the partial vapour pressure of each component in the solution is directly proportional to its mole fraction in the solution. Mathematically, for components A and B: p_A = x_A × p°_A and p_B = x_B × p°_B, where p°_A and p°_B are the vapour pressures of pure A and pure B respectively, and x_A, x_B are their mole fractions. The total vapour pressure of the solution is p_total = p_A + p_B = x_A·p°_A + x_B·p°_B.

sub_questions.text: (ख)(ii) राउल्ट का नियम हेनरी के नियम की एक विशेष स्थिति है। टिप्पणी कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b)(ii) Raoult's law is a special case of Henry's law. Comment.

key_points: Both laws express partial pressure as proportional to mole fraction; in Raoult's law the proportionality constant is the vapour pressure of the pure solvent (p°), while in Henry's law it is KH. When the solute is the same as the solvent, KH = p°, and Raoult's law is obtained as a special case.

sub_questions.solution: Henry's law states: p = KH × x, where KH is Henry's law constant and x is the mole fraction of the dissolved gas. Raoult's law states: p = p° × x, where p° is the vapour pressure of the pure component. Both laws express partial pressure as directly proportional to the mole fraction. Raoult's law is thus a special case of Henry's law in which the Henry's law constant KH equals the vapour pressure of the pure component p°. This equality holds when solute and solvent are chemically identical (e.g., the pure liquid itself), making Raoult's law a special form of Henry's law applicable to the solvent.

sub_questions.text: (ग) आदर्श विलयन के दो लक्षण लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (c) Write two characteristics of an ideal solution.

key_points: 1. Obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentrations.
2. ΔHmix = 0 and ΔVmix = 0 (no heat evolved/absorbed and no change in volume on mixing).

sub_questions.solution: Two characteristics of an ideal solution are: (1) It obeys Raoult's law over the entire range of concentrations, meaning the partial vapour pressure of each component equals its mole fraction multiplied by the vapour pressure of the pure component. (2) The enthalpy of mixing is zero (ΔHmix = 0), meaning no heat is absorbed or released during the formation of the solution, and the volume change on mixing is also zero (ΔVmix = 0), indicating that the interactions between solute–solvent molecules are the same as solute–solute and solvent–solvent interactions.

questions.text: (क)(i) प्रथम कोटि की अभिक्रिया N2O5(g) → 2NO2(g) + ½O2(g) के लिए N2O5 की प्रारंभिक सांद्रता 1·2 × 10⁻2 mol L⁻1 थी। 60 मिनट के पश्चात N2O5 की सांद्रता 0·2 × 10⁻2 mol L⁻1 थी। 318 K पर अभिक्रिया का वेग स्थिरांक परिकलित कीजिए। [log 6 = 0·778] (ii) निम्नलिखित के लिए कारण दीजिए : (I) हम संतुलित रासायनिक समीकरण के आधार पर किसी अभिक्रिया की कोटि ज्ञात नहीं कर सकते। (II) कोई द्वि-अणुक अभिक्रिया विशिष्ट परिस्थिति में गतिकत: प्रथम कोटि की हो सकती है।
questions.text_english: (a)(i) The initial concentration of N2O5 in the first order reaction : N2O5(g) → 2NO2(g) + ½O2(g) was 1·2 × 10⁻2 mol L⁻1. The concentration of N2O5 after 60 minutes was 0·2 × 10⁻2 mol L⁻1. Calculate the rate constant of the reaction at 318 K. [log 6 = 0·778]. (ii) Account for the following : (I) We cannot determine the order of a reaction by taking into consideration the balanced chemical equation. (II) A bimolecular reaction may become kinetically of first order under a specified condition.

sub_questions.text: (ख)(i) 298 K से परम ताप में 10 K की वृद्धि के साथ किसी रासायनिक अभिक्रिया का वेग दुगुना हो जाता है। सक्रियण ऊर्जा (Ea) की गणना कीजिए। [2·303 R = 19·15 JK⁻1 mol⁻1, log 2 = 0·3] (ii) अभिक्रिया 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2 के लिए प्रस्तावित क्रियाविधि : (I) H2O2 + I⁻ → H2O + IO⁻ (मन्द); (II) H2O2 + IO⁻ → H2O + I⁻ + O2 (तीव्र) | (1) अभिक्रिया के लिए वेग नियम लिखिए। (2) अभिक्रिया की समग्र कोटि एवं आण्विकता लिखिए।
sub_questions.text_english: (b)(i) The rate of the chemical reaction doubles for an increase of 10 K in absolute temperature from 298 K. Calculate activation energy (Ea). [2.303 R = 19.15 JK⁻1 mol⁻1, log 2 = 0.3]. (ii) For reaction 2H2O2 → 2H2O + O2, mechanism: (I) H2O2 + I⁻ → H2O + IO⁻ (slow); (II) H2O2 + IO⁻ → H2O + I⁻ + O2 (fast). (1) Write rate law. (2) Write overall order and molecularity.

key_points: Ea ≈ 52,897 J mol⁻1 ≈ 52.9 kJ mol⁻1
Rate law: Rate = k[H2O2][I⁻]
Overall order = 2; Molecularity of rate-determining step = 2

sub_questions.solution: Part (b)(i): Using the Arrhenius equation: log(k2/k1) = Ea/(2.303R) × (T2 − T1)/(T1×T2). Here k2/k1 = 2, T1 = 298 K, T2 = 308 K, so log 2 = Ea/(19.15) × 10/(298×308). Therefore 0.3 = Ea/19.15 × 10/91784. Ea = 0.3 × 19.15 × 91784/10 = 0.3 × 175,786 ≈ 52,736 J mol⁻1 ≈ 52.7 kJ mol⁻1. Part (b)(ii): (1) Rate law is determined by the slow (rate-determining) step: Rate = k[H2O2][I⁻]. (2) The overall order of the reaction is 2 (first order in H2O2 and first order in I⁻). The molecularity of the rate-determining step (I) is 2, as it involves two molecules (H2O2 and I⁻).

key_points: Order cannot be determined from balanced equation as it depends on mechanism.
Pseudo first order occurs when one reactant is in large excess.

questions.solution: Part (a)(i): For a first-order reaction, k = (2.303/t) × log([A]0/[A]t). Here t = 60 min, [A]0 = 1.2 × 10⁻2 mol L⁻1, [A]t = 0.2 × 10⁻2 mol L⁻1. Therefore k = (2.303/60) × log(1.2/0.2) = (2.303/60) × log 6 = (2.303/60) × 0.778 = 1.792/60 = 0.02987 min⁻1 ≈ 2.99 × 10⁻2 min⁻1. Part (a)(ii)(I): The order of a reaction cannot be determined from the balanced chemical equation because the order depends on the mechanism (the rate-determining step), not on the overall stoichiometry. A reaction may involve multiple elementary steps, and the slowest step determines the rate law. Part (a)(ii)(II): A bimolecular reaction involves two molecules in its rate-determining step. If one of the reactants is present in a large excess (e.g., the solvent or water), its concentration remains essentially constant throughout the reaction. In that case, the rate law simplifies from Rate = k[A][B] to Rate = k’[A], where k’ = k[B]constant. This gives a first-order (pseudo first-order) kinetics, even though the reaction is fundamentally bimolecular.

(II) Reagent: O3 then Zn/H2O (ozonolysis), or specific oxidant

sub_questions.solution: Part (b)(i): (I) Ethylbenzene reacts with KMnO4/KOH followed by H3O+ to give benzoic acid (C6H5COOH) — the side chain is oxidised regardless of its length to give –COOH. (II) To convert cyclohexylidene=CH2 to cyclohexanecarbaldehyde, the reagent is ozone (O3) followed by reductive workup Zn/H2O (ozonolysis), which cleaves the C=C double bond to give the aldehyde. (III) The compound 4-oxocyclohexanecarbaldehyde contains an aldehyde group; with Tollens' reagent [Ag(NH3)2]+, the aldehyde is oxidised to the carboxylate (silver mirror deposited), giving 4-oxocyclohexanecarboxylic acid as the organic product. Part (b)(ii): (I) Benzaldehyde to benzophenone: React benzaldehyde with phenylmagnesium bromide (C6H5MgBr) in ether to give C6H5CH(OH)C6H5 (benzhydrol), then oxidise with PCC or acidified KMnO4 to benzophenone (C6H5COC6H5). (II) Benzaldehyde to 3-phenyl propanol: Perform an aldol condensation of benzaldehyde with acetaldehyde to get cinnamaldehyde (C6H5CH=CHCHO), then reduce with LiAlH4 or NaBH4 to get 3-phenyl propanol (C6H5CH2CH2CH2OH).

key_points: (I) Cyclopentanone + semicarbazide (H2NCONHNH2) → cyclopentanone semicarbazone
(II) (CH3)2Cd + 2CH3COCl → 2CH3COCH3 (acetone) + CdCl2
(III) Benzoyl chloride + H2/Pd–BaSO4 (Rosenmund reduction) → benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO)
Test I: NaHCO3 solution — benzoic acid gives brisk effervescence (CO2), ethyl benzoate does not.
Test II: Tollens' or Fehling's test — propanal gives silver mirror/brick red precipitate; propanone does not.

questions.solution: Part (a)(i): (I) Cyclopentanone reacts with semicarbazide (H2NCONHNH2) to form cyclopentanone semicarbazone — the C=O condenses with –NH2 to give C=N–NHCONH2 with loss of water. (II) (CH3)2Cd reacts with 2 equivalents of acetyl chloride (CH3COCl) in a nucleophilic addition reaction to give 2 molecules of acetone (CH3COCH3) and CdCl2. This is the Gilman-type organocadmium reaction used to prepare symmetrical ketones from acid chlorides. (III) Benzoyl chloride (C6H5COCl) undergoes Rosenmund reduction with H2 over poisoned Pd–BaSO4 catalyst to give benzaldehyde (C6H5CHO) — the acid chloride is selectively reduced to aldehyde without over-reduction. Part (a)(ii): (I) To distinguish ethyl benzoate and benzoic acid: add sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO3) solution — benzoic acid being a carboxylic acid reacts with NaHCO3 to give brisk effervescence of CO2, while ethyl benzoate (an ester) does not react with NaHCO3. (II) To distinguish propanal (an aldehyde) and propanone (a ketone): add Tollens' reagent (ammoniacal AgNO3) — propanal gives a shiny silver mirror on the walls of the test tube, while propanone does not react. Alternatively, Fehling's solution gives a brick-red precipitate with propanal but not propanone.

questions.text: (क)(i) कारण दीजिए : (I) [Ni(CO)4] प्रतिचुम्बकीय है जबकि [NiCl4]2– अनुचुम्बकीय है। [परमाणु क्रमांक : Ni = 28] (II) NH3 की तुलना में CO एक प्रबल संकुलन कर्मक है। (III) संकुल [Co(en)2Cl2]+ का विपक्ष समावयव ध्रुवण अघूर्णक है। (ii) क्रिस्टल क्षेत्र सिद्धांत का उपयोग करते हुए Fe3+ के अष्टफलकीय संकुलों में निम्नलिखित की उपस्थिति में अयुगलित इलेक्ट्रॉनों की संख्या लिखिए : (I) प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगन्ड; (II) दुर्बल क्षेत्र लिगन्ड। [परमाणु क्रमांक : Fe = 26]
questions.text_english: (a)(i) Give reasons : (I) [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic whereas [NiCl4]2– is paramagnetic. [Atomic number : Ni = 28] (II) CO is a stronger complexing agent than NH3. (III) The trans isomer of complex [Co(en)2Cl2]+ is optically inactive. (ii) Using Crystal Field theory, write the number of unpaired electrons in octahedral complexes of Fe3+ in the presence of : (I) Strong field ligand; (II) Weak field ligand. [Atomic number : Fe = 26]

sub_questions.text: (ख)(i) निम्नलिखित यौगिकों द्वारा प्रदर्शित समावयवता के प्रकार का नाम लिखिए। उनके संगत समावयवों का चित्र भी बनाइए : (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6]; (II) [Co(en)3]3+; (III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3]. (ii) दुर्बल क्षेत्र और प्रबल क्षेत्र लिगन्डों के बीच अन्तर स्पष्ट कीजिए। लिगन्ड की प्रबलता किस प्रकार संकुल के प्रचक्रण को प्रभावित करती है ?
sub_questions.text_english: (b)(i) Name the type of isomerism exhibited by the following compounds. Also draw their corresponding isomers : (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6]; (II) [Co(en)3]3+; (III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3]. (ii) Differentiate between weak field and strong field ligands. How does the strength of the ligand influence the spin of the complex?

key_points: (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] shows ionisation isomerism: isomers are [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] and [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6].
(II) [Co(en)3]3+ shows optical isomerism (d and l enantiomers).
(III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] shows geometrical isomerism (facial and meridional isomers).
Weak field ligands: cause small crystal field splitting, electrons remain unpaired (high spin). Strong field ligands: cause large splitting, electrons pair up (low spin).

sub_questions.solution: Part (b)(i): (I) [Co(NH3)6][Cr(CN)6] exhibits ionisation isomerism (also called coordination isomerism). The isomer is [Cr(NH3)6][Co(CN)6], where the cationic and anionic complex units exchange their ligands. (II) [Co(en)3]3+ exhibits optical isomerism (enantiomerism). Since en is a bidentate ligand and the complex has no plane of symmetry, it exists as two non-superimposable mirror images (d- and l-forms). (III) [Co(NH3)3(NO2)3] exhibits geometrical isomerism: the facial (fac) isomer has the three identical ligands on one face of the octahedron, while the meridional (mer) isomer has them in a plane containing the metal ion. Part (b)(ii): Weak field ligands (e.g., Cl⁻, F⁻, Br⁻, I⁻, H2O) cause a small crystal field splitting energy (Δo). When Δo is smaller than the pairing energy, electrons prefer to remain unpaired and fill all the d orbitals singly first (high-spin complex, more unpaired electrons). Strong field ligands (e.g., CO, CN⁻, en, NH3) cause a large Δo. When Δo is greater than the pairing energy, electrons pair up in the lower t2g orbitals before filling the eg orbitals (low-spin complex, fewer unpaired electrons). Thus, the strength of the ligand determines whether the complex is high-spin or low-spin.

key_points: (I) [Ni(CO)4]: CO is a strong field ligand causing 3d8 electrons to pair completely into sp3 hybridisation (tetrahedral), leaving no unpaired electrons — diamagnetic. [NiCl4]2–: Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand, so hybridisation is sp3 with 2 unpaired electrons — paramagnetic.
(II) CO acts as both a σ donor and π acceptor (back-bonding from d orbitals into CO π* orbitals), stabilising the complex far more than NH3 which is only a σ donor.
(III) The trans-[Co(en)2Cl2]+ has a plane of symmetry (the plane containing Co, the two Cl, and the midpoints of the two en ligands), making it achiral — optically inactive.
Fe3+ is [Ar]3d5. With strong field ligand: all 5 electrons pair in t2g — 1 unpaired electron. With weak field ligand: all 5 d orbitals singly occupied — 5 unpaired electrons.

questions.solution: Part (a)(i): (I) Ni (Z=28) has electronic configuration [Ar]3d84s2, so Ni(0) in [Ni(CO)4] has configuration 3d104s0 (electrons rearrange in the presence of strong field CO ligands). All electrons are paired in the 3d10 configuration, so [Ni(CO)4] is diamagnetic. In [NiCl4]2–, Ni is in +2 state with 3d8 configuration. Cl⁻ is a weak field ligand, so no pairing occurs and sp3 hybridisation gives 2 unpaired electrons, making [NiCl4]2– paramagnetic. (II) CO is a stronger complexing agent than NH3 because CO acts as both a σ-donor (donates a lone pair to the metal) and a π-acceptor (accepts electron density from filled metal d-orbitals into its empty π* antibonding orbital — back-bonding). This synergic bonding (synergism) greatly stabilises the metal-ligand bond. NH3 is only a σ-donor and lacks the ability to accept π electron density, so it forms weaker complexes. (III) The trans isomer of [Co(en)2Cl2]+ has a plane of symmetry bisecting the en groups and passing through Co and the two Cl atoms. Due to this plane of symmetry, the trans isomer is superimposable on its mirror image — it is achiral and therefore optically inactive (cannot rotate plane-polarised light). Part (a)(ii): Fe3+ has configuration [Ar]3d5. (I) With a strong field ligand (large Δo > pairing energy), the 5 d-electrons pair up in the t2g orbitals: t2g5 eg0 — giving 1 unpaired electron (low spin). (II) With a weak field ligand (small Δo < pairing energy), the electrons remain unpaired following Hund's rule: t2g3 eg2 — giving 5 unpaired electrons (high spin).
